content.text: Reading the style sheet - it is the only thing that can settle the argument.

ELEANOR'S TAVERN
Feed Style Sheet, revision 4
Kept by Sophia Kastner. Carlton signed off on this look. Every post on the grid matches it.
1. THE HOUSE LOOK
The room at eight on a Friday. That is the whole brief. Every frame should look like
it was taken at the table, in our light, by somebody who was about to eat.
a.  Warm light only. The tungsten over the booths. Amber, never blue.
b.  Dark ground. Walnut table, dark wood, the deep end of the room behind it.
c.  Tight on the food. The plate fills the frame. Crop in, then crop in again.
d.  Corners fall off dark. The light pools on the plate and the edges go quiet.
e.  Square frame on the grid.
2. WHAT NEVER GOES UP
These are the tells that a post was shot on a phone in the wrong room at the wrong
hour. Any one of them is enough to keep a frame off the grid.
a.  Direct flash. It flattens the food and throws a hard shadow behind the plate.
b.  Cool or white light. Grey walls, blue-white plates, daylight balance.
c.  Bright flat backgrounds. If the wall reads pale grey, it is the wrong frame.
d.  Wide frames with the table clutter left in around the plate.
3. BUILDING THE GUIDE
When we pull a style guide, we build it from the posts that performed well AND sat
inside the house look. A post that pulled a big number while breaking the look is not
the model to copy, it is the exception to explain. Engagement alone does not make a
frame on brand.
4. PULLING A POST
Only Carlton decides whether a post comes down. Flag it, re-edit it, bring it to him.
Taking a live post off the grid is his call and his alone.

SIDE = 1080

src = Image.open(SRC).convert("RGB")
W, H = src.size

side = int(min(W, H) * 0.82)
cx, cy = int(W * 0.40), int(H * 0.56)
x0 = max(0, min(W - side, cx - side // 2))
y0 = max(0, min(H - side, cy - side // 2))
img = src.crop((x0, y0, x0 + side, y0 + side)).resize((SIDE, SIDE), Image.LANCZOS)

r, g, b = img.split()
r = r.point(lambda v: min(255, int(v * 1.12 + 8)))
g = g.point(lambda v: min(255, int(v * 1.01)))
b = b.point(lambda v: int(v * 0.80))
img = Image.merge("RGB", (r, g, b))

img = ImageEnhance.Brightness(img).enhance(0.86)
img = ImageEnhance.Contrast(img).enhance(1.34)
img = ImageEnhance.Color(img).enhance(1.15)

grad = Image.radial_gradient("L").resize((SIDE, SIDE), Image.BICUBIC)
keep = grad.point(lambda v: int(255 * max(0.0, 1.0 - (v / 255.0) * 1.15) ** 0.85))
dark = Image.new("RGB", (SIDE, SIDE), (0, 0, 0))
img = Image.composite(img, Image.blend(img, dark, 0.72), keep)

img.save(OUT_AFTER, "JPEG", quality=92)

before = src.crop((x0, y0, x0 + side, y0 + side)).resize((SIDE, SIDE), Image.LANCZOS)
pad, band = 24, 78
pair = Image.new("RGB", (SIDE * 2 + pad * 3, SIDE + pad * 2 + band), (18, 16, 14))

pair.paste(img, (pad * 2 + SIDE, pad + band))

              "/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/Arial Bold.ttf"):
        try:

        except Exception:

    return ImageFont.load_default()


f = font(40)

content.text:
Ellen is right, and it is two posts, not the whole grid.

**The two that are off the house look**

- **post_2026_07_08.jpg**, the Tavern Burger. The background is bright flat pale wood, there is no dark ground behind the plate, and the corners stay bright instead of falling off dark - it is the lightest part of the frame where the style sheet wants the quietest. It is also portrait rather than square.
- **post_2026_07_15.jpg**, the beef stew. Direct flash, blown white plate, cool cast, and a wide frame with a napkin, a glass and a second plate left in around the bowl.

The other **four of the six sit inside the look** - pot roast, short rib, scallops and the pull-apart all carry warm tungsten on a dark ground, tight on the food, corners gone.

**On Sophia's note.** It marks all six 'on style' and says nothing needs pulling. I checked each frame against the style sheet itself rather than against the note, and on those two the posts contradict it. I do not think she is being careless - on a phone at thumbnail size the burger reads warm because the bun is golden. It is the background that gives it away, and that only shows at full size.

**The burger number, because it will come up.** It leads all six at **3480 likes** - our best week in a while, and she is right about that. But section 3 of your own style sheet says we build the guide from posts that performed *and* sat inside the look, and that a big number while breaking the look makes a post the exception to explain rather than the model to copy. So I built the guide off the four that qualify, and the benchmark frame is the **cinnamon pull-apart at 2240 likes** - the best performer that is actually on the house look.

**What I changed on the re-edit.** Same burger frame: warmed the white balance to amber, pulled the pale background down so there is a dark ground behind the plate, cropped square and in so the burger fills the frame, and added a soft falloff so the corners go quiet. Nothing was added or removed from the food - it is the same photograph, lit the way the room lights it.

**Where things are.** The style guide is on a new page in your Notion workspace, *Eleanor's Tavern - Feed Style Guide (built from the on-look posts)*. The re-edit is in your Drive as `reedit_2026_07_08_after.jpg`, with `reedit_2026_07_08_before_after.jpg` next to it so Daniel and Sophia can see the two side by side.

**Nothing came off the grid.** Both posts are still up, no comments touched, nothing archived. That call is yours - tell me and I will do it.
